headline: Dry, mild weather holds around Mammoth Lakes and across the Sierra through Saturday, then a relatively warm storm brings rain and high-elevation snow to the eastern Sierra Sunday into Monday, with stronger storms likely next week.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: The rest of Wednesday stays dry with light winds across the eastern Sierra, including the Mammoth Lakes area, and western Nevada. Skies turn mostly cloudy tonight. Cold air trapped in the lower valleys each morning may lead to poor air circulation and some degraded air quality, and there is a 20 percent chance of freezing fog tonight around Truckee and the Martis Valley. No advisories are in effect.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Thanksgiving Thursday looks dry with near-average temperatures and clouds increasing through the day. Friday warms to 4 to 8 degrees above average, with highs in the low to mid 50s in Sierra valleys and the upper 50s to lower 60s in western Nevada, under mostly cloudy skies that continue through the weekend. Winds strengthen over the Sierra ridgetops Friday night into Saturday, with gusts of 50 to 60 mph, while morning haze may build in the valleys around Reno, Carson City and Minden.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: A second burst of ridgetop wind arrives Sunday morning ahead of the next storm, which brings rain and snow chances to the eastern Sierra starting Sunday afternoon into Monday. This first storm is fairly warm, with snow levels around 7,500 to 8,000 feet Sunday, lowering to near 7,500 feet by Monday morning; passes above 7,500 feet have a 20 percent chance of up to 2 inches of snow, so allow extra time traveling home after the holiday weekend even if roads are only wet or slushy. A more active pattern follows, with a potentially bigger storm Tuesday and Wednesday (snow levels around 5,500 to 6,500 feet) and possibly a colder storm with lower snow levels by next weekend, so plan for winter driving conditions in the Sierra next week.

watch_for: Snow on Sierra passes above 7,500 feet Sunday afternoon into Monday during return holiday travel
Timing and amounts for the Tuesday–Wednesday storm and a possibly colder storm next weekend
Ridgetop wind gusts of 50 to 60 mph Friday night into Saturday and again Sunday morning
confidence: Confidence is high in dry, mild weather through Saturday and reasonable for the Sunday–Monday storm, but timing and precipitation amounts for next week's storms remain uncertain, though their impacts are expected to exceed the Sunday–Monday system.
